intro.title: Welcome to Imilchil — lakes and high plateaus
intro.p1: Imilchil is a high Atlas village known for the twin lakes Isli and Tislit, wide mountain plateaus and strong Amazigh traditions. It sits far from the main tourist circuits, on roads that reward travellers who accept distance and altitude.
intro.p2: Plan one or two nights for the lakes, highland light and village life. The famous marriage festival (moussem) draws crowds in season; outside those days the area is quiet and elemental. Check road conditions before you go — winter and early spring can close high passes.

lakes.title: Lakes Isli & Tislit
lakes.p1: Isli and Tislit are Imilchil’s signature landscape: two high lakes set in open mountain country, tied to a local legend of star-crossed lovers and still the main reason many travellers climb this far.
lakes.p2: Walk the shores, take in the light and dress for wind. Paths are simple; facilities are limited. Respect the shore environment.
lakes.tip: Clear mornings after rain or snowmelt give the strongest colours on the water.

village.title: Imilchil village
village.p1: The village is a working highland centre: small shops, basic services and a pace set by altitude and seasons rather than tourism.
village.p2: Use it as a base for the lakes and plateau walks. Expect simple infrastructure and warm but reserved hospitality.
village.tip: Arrive with cash; card payment is not always available.

moussem.title: Marriage festival (moussem)
moussem.p1: Imilchil’s moussem of marriage is one of Morocco’s best-known traditional gatherings: families, music, dress and the historic role of the festival in matchmaking among Amazigh communities of the region.
moussem.p2: Dates shift with the calendar and local organisation. Outside festival days the village returns to quiet highland life — visit for culture, not only for the event.
moussem.tip: If you aim for the moussem, confirm dates locally or with recent travellers; crowds and lodging fill early.

plateau.title: High plateaus
plateau.p1: Around Imilchil the land opens into high plateaus and grazings — big skies, sparse settlements and a strong sense of altitude.
plateau.p2: Short walks from the road or village edges are enough for most visitors; weather changes fast.
plateau.tip: Windproof layers matter even in summer afternoons.

valleys.title: Surrounding valleys
valleys.p1: Valleys fold down from the plateaus toward the lakes and lower tracks — greener pockets, small plots and the routes locals use between villages.
valleys.p2: Explore with respect for private land and livestock. A local driver or guide helps on rougher tracks.
valleys.tip: Late afternoon light on the valley sides is often the best of the day.

traditions.title: Amazigh highland life
traditions.p1: Imilchil sits in a region of strong Amazigh identity: language, dress, seasonal markets and community life shaped by the high Atlas.
traditions.p2: Observe and ask before photographing people. Markets and festival days show the culture at its most visible.
traditions.tip: Learning a few Tamazight greetings is appreciated.

q1.question: How long should I stay in Imilchil?
q1.answer: One night covers the lakes and village; two nights if you want plateau walks or to be present for festival days.

q2.question: What are Lakes Isli and Tislit?
q2.answer: Two high-altitude lakes near Imilchil, linked in local legend and the main natural draw of the area.

q3.question: How do I get to Imilchil?
q3.answer: By mountain road, typically via Midelt or Rich. Conditions vary; a suitable vehicle and local advice are important.

q4.question: When is the marriage festival?
q4.answer: Dates change with the year and local organisation. Confirm in advance if the moussem is your reason to visit; book lodging early.

itinerary.title: Suggested 2–3 Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: A balanced plan for the lakes, village life and highland light.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Reach Imilchil, check into a simple auberge, orient in the village.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Drive or walk to the twin lakes for shore time and mountain light.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Tagine or local plate and a cold highland night.
detailed_itinerary.day2_m: Morning — Plateau or second lake visit
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Open highland walk or return to the lakes in softer light.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Market, cafés and a slower look at Amazigh highland life.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Simple dinner and early sleep at altitude.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Coffee and a last look at the plateau before the mountain road.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Descend toward Midelt for the Fez/Errachidia corridor, or continue on regional mountain roads.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Overnight in Midelt or further on your Atlas itinerary.
